newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ANGRY BELGIAN PHILIPS STAFF OCCUPY PLANT.
newsitem.headline: ANGRY BELGIAN PHILIPS STAFF OCCUPY PLANT.

text.p: Staff at the Philips Electronics NV television plant in Bruges, Belgium, occupied their premises on Thursday in anger over job losses resulting from a restructuring of Philips television operations.
"We are not going to accept this," a union spokesman said.

The job cuts are part of a wider restructuring of the Sound and Vision division of the Dutch electronics group, which also affects sites in France and Italy. It involves the number of jobs at the sites falling by 50 percent to around 1,400.
The union spokesman said staff had adjusted well to market demands recently and were now being unfairly treated.
Staff levels had already been cut in November 1995 when 70 jobs were lost.
Under the current plan seven in 10 blue-collar jobs were to go and one in three white-collar jobs, he said.
The union spokesman said any further action would be decided at a meeting on Monday.

A Philips Bruges spokesman said Philips could not afford to make the same products at different places and noted that in the new strategy Philips Bruges had been assigned an "important and essential task", which was development and production.
In the restructuring Bruges will be the world-wide high-end colour television development centre with a production facility.

Philips said in July that developments in the consumer electionics industry meant a restructuring was needed, especially in Europe. Sound and Vision comprises television, audio, video equipment and interactive media systems.
Together with this latest restructuring some 2,500 jobs are being cut in the division's industrial activities in western Europe.
Philips employs 270,000 people in 60 countries. The consumer products division, which includes Sound and Vision, employed a total workforce of over 70,000 as at end-June.
